input: In order to maintain reliable availability of a packaging film while at the same time avoiding the excessive holding of stock, an appropriate safety stock level needs to be established for the item. Demand for the film averages 1933 units per week, although it fluctuates considerably from week to week, with a standard deviation of 435 units per week. The replenishment lead time for the film is 2 weeks, which means that any order placed takes some time to arrive, and it is during this window that the safety stock has to provide its protection. The policy adopted here targets a 95% cycle service level, which is to say that in 95% of replenishment cycles, demand should be met without running out of stock. Working through the calculation on this basis, the safety stock comes out at 1015 units. In arriving at this figure, demand has been treated as though it were normally distributed and independent from one week to the next, and it is worth pointing out that seasonal peaks in demand have been left out of the picture altogether, so the 1015 units should be read with that important qualification in mind.
target:
Set the safety stock for the packaging film at 1015 units. The figure is the planning team's to hold and review.

Safety stock covers the variation in demand over the replenishment lead time. Demand for the film averages 1933 units per week with a standard deviation of 435 units per week, and the lead time is 2 weeks. The policy target is a 95% cycle service level: in 95% of replenishment cycles, demand is met without a stockout. On the stated demand figures and that service target, the safety stock is 1015 units.

The level is a policy figure, not a forecast for any particular week. In most cycles the stock is untouched; it is drawn on in the cycles where demand over the lead time ran above its mean. A higher service target returns a higher stock on the same demand figures; the target is where the cost of holding film is set against the cost of a stockout, and that choice belongs to the business.

The figure rests on its basis, and the basis has a named limit: demand is treated as normal and independent between weeks, and seasonal peaks are excluded. A seasonal peak is exactly the week in which demand departs from that basis, and the stock set here is not sized for it. The level should be revisited when the demand pattern changes, not after a stockout has shown the change.
